sources.title: GPT-5.1: A smarter, more conversational ChatGPT
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27, 2026. The November 12, 2025 release starts public rollout of GPT-5.1 Thinking and Instant in ChatGPT and explicitly maps Thinking to the forthcoming GPT-5.1 API model, separate from Instant and Auto routing. It publishes no total or active parameter count.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.1 for developers
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27, 2026. The November 13 API announcement describes adaptive reasoning, optional no-reasoning mode, 24-hour prompt caching and model-generated apply_patch and shell tool calls, but no model-size or active-parameter specification. Changes in reasoning tokens and latency do not quantify model parameters.

sources.title: GPT-5.1 model documentation (Markdown)
sources.evidence: Fresh exact-model documentation fetched and read October 27, 2026, including the successful HTTP 200 Markdown cache fetched at 16:22 UTC. It binds gpt-5.1 to gpt-5.1-2025-11-13 and lists 400,000 context, 128,000 maximum output, text/image input, text output, reasoning support, none/low/medium/high effort, hosted endpoints, function calling, uploads and caching. Neither total nor active parameters are published; API configuration parameters and token limits are not weight counts.

sources.title: GPT-5.1 Instant and GPT-5.1 Thinking System Card Addendum
sources.evidence: Original November 12, 2025 card freshly read from the October 27 HTTP 200 PDF cache. It identifies gpt-5.1-thinking separately from gpt-5.1-instant, describes adaptive reasoning and reports safety/image-input evaluations. Its five-page full text contains no nominal total or active parameter disclosure or dense/MoE specification.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Archived guide explicitly applies to models before GPT-5.6. It explains caching as reusing key/value projections in Transformer attention layers and includes an exact gpt-5.1 extended-cache request. Combined with exact-model caching support, this supports a qualified broad Transformer inference, not dense/MoE structure or a complete block inventory.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses accepts PDF file inputs; for vision-capable models, the API sends extracted text and page images to the model. Chat Completions also accepts PDF file content. Applied to GPT-5.1’s documented vision, file upload and endpoint support, this establishes PDF as an API input format, not another native sensory modality.

sources.title: Update to GPT-5 System Card: GPT-5.2
sources.evidence: Freshly rechecked the October 27 HTTP 200 original PDF. The December 11, 2025 report includes exact gpt-5.1-thinking comparison columns, but these measure safety and benchmark performance, not model size or activated parameters. It warns that comparison values can use later versions of previously launched models.

sources.title: Reasoning Models Struggle to Control their Chains of Thought
sources.evidence: Freshly rechecked the October 27 HTTP 200 original PDF. GPT-5.1 appears among the 13 reasoning models and in Table 2, but Figure 1b and the size-scaling discussion use GPT-OSS and Qwen open-weight models; the separate 7B RL intervention uses Olmo. None of those sizes specifies GPT-5.1 total or active parameters.

sources.title: Sidestepping Evaluation Awareness and Anticipating Misalignment with Production Evaluations
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27, 2026. First-party research studies GPT-5.1 deployment behavior and a training-time reward bug involving superficial web-tool use. This is model-specific training evidence but does not disclose its total or active parameters, dense/MoE routing or complete architecture.

sources.title: API deprecations
sources.evidence: The October 1, 2026 notice schedules gpt-5.1 and gpt-5.1-2025-11-13 API shutdown for April 1, 2027. The deprecated designation therefore does not mean this endpoint was already shut down at review time.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Sections 3.3 and 9.1 restrict model extraction/reverse engineering and grant limited service access without transferring IP rights in the service. Together with the exact hosted release, this supports the descriptive Proprietary classification, not an open checkpoint license.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
sources.evidence: Freshly rechecked the October 27 HTTP 200 original PDF linked from this system-card page. Table 6 includes an exact gpt-5.1 column with HealthBench scores and response lengths; these are not parameter counts. Model-specific calculator-hacking discussion also concerns behavior, and no nominal total or active parameter count is supplied.

sources.title: CaveAgent: Transforming LLMs into Stateful Runtime Operators (v4, June 29, 2026)
sources.publisher: Maohao Ran et al. / CaveAgent research team
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27, 2026. Section 4.1 and Table 3 identify GPT-5.1 exactly and mark both Size and Arch. as N/A. The caption explicitly defines N/A as parameter count or architecture not publicly disclosed, while other rows report total and active counts separately. This is the original research team's comparison, not an OpenAI disclosure; N/A means unavailable here, not zero or inapplicable. The original v1 was also checked; it supplies counts for open models but no GPT-5.1 count. The OpenReview PDF endpoint returned a browser challenge, so the full arXiv v4 table was used.

name.note: Official API display name; this record tracks the Thinking model, not Instant/Chat or the Auto router.

developer.note: First-party release and authored system card identify OpenAI.

family.note: Use the GPT-5.1 release family for this model and its related variants; the announcement places this iteration within the broader GPT-5 generation.

release_date.note: Earliest public GPT-5.1 Thinking rollout was November 12 in ChatGPT. The same announcement explicitly identifies its forthcoming API name as GPT-5.1. API access and the dated gpt-5.1-2025-11-13 snapshot followed November 13; the catalog records the earlier named-model release.

open_weights.note: Released through hosted ChatGPT and API access, with no public GPT-5.1 checkpoint distribution identified. The reviewed access terms grant service use rather than model ownership or an open-weight license.

license.note: Descriptive classification of hosted model/service access; not an SPDX checkpoint license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit of both original releases, exact API specification, original system card, later OpenAI comparison/training research and targeted total/active-count searches found no published nominal GPT-5.1 total. CaveAgent v4 Table 3 independently marks the exact model's size N/A and defines this as undisclosed. No explicitly named, disclosed-size base model was established for a lineage inference. This is a bounded source review, not proof of universal absence.

active_parameters_b.note: Freshly checked separately from total: no nominal activated-parameter count was found in the exact-model specifications or later original comparisons. CaveAgent v4 Table 3 reports total/active conventions for open models but N/A for GPT-5.1. Adaptive reasoning changes token use and thinking time, not a disclosed active-weight count. Neither dense total=active equality, sibling sizes nor black-box capacity estimates are used.

architecture.note: Qualified operational inference: exact GPT-5.1 launch and documentation support prompt caching, and the pre-GPT-5.6 technical guide includes gpt-5.1 while explaining attention-layer key/value caching in Transformer layers. This establishes broad Transformer-based attention, not exclusively Transformer blocks, dense/MoE routing, dimensions or a complete architecture specification.

context_window.note: Exact API model documentation lists a 400,000-token context window and separately 128,000 maximum output tokens. These are API specifications; do not add the two or substitute ChatGPT product limits.

modalities.note: Exact model supports text/image input and text output. PDF denotes the documented API file path that extracts text and page images for a vision model; it does not assert native PDF sensing, audio input or audio output.

reasoning.note: GPT-5.1 Thinking/API supports reasoning tokens and configurable low/medium/high effort. The default none setting disables reasoning for a request; it does not make this a non-reasoning-only model.

tool_call.note: Exact model documents function calling and Responses tools; original release also demonstrates model-generated apply_patch and shell calls.

patch.notes: GPT-5.1 Thinking first rolled out in ChatGPT on November 12, 2025; the API release and default gpt-5.1-2025-11-13 snapshot followed November 13. This record is separate from GPT-5.1 Instant (gpt-5.1-chat-latest) and Auto routing. API specifications are 400K context and 128K maximum output; reasoning effort supports none (default), low, medium and high. PDF input is processed into text and page images by the API. Transformer is a qualified inference from exact-model prompt caching and the documented pre-GPT-5.6 attention KV mechanism; the full block inventory and dense/MoE routing remain undisclosed. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed; the original CaveAgent comparison also marks GPT-5.1's size unavailable. The API model is deprecated with shutdown announced for April 1, 2027, still in the future at review time.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit reopened the original GPT-5.1 releases and specification, read the launch card and later OpenAI comparisons/research, and searched for newer total and active disclosures separately. Added CaveAgent v4 Table 3, whose exact GPT-5.1 row explicitly reports size and architecture as undisclosed. Both parameter values remain null with explicit patches; no supported nominal size or named-base size inference was found. Preserved the other twelve assessments, including release chronology, API capabilities and the qualified Transformer inference.
